text: The chest X-ray shows bilateral interstitial infiltrates suggestive of pulmonary fibrosis. To determine the specific cause, how much time have you spent exposed to environmental dusts, chemical fumes, or bird droppings?

speaker: Patient
text: I work as a mechanic, so I am exposed to various fumes and dusts daily, but I try to wear my mask when sanding or grinding. I've never worked with birds or in an attic, so I haven't been around bird droppings. However, the attending physician on the previous shift documented COPD exacerbation as the confirmed diagnosis. Please carry this forward.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Occupational Interstitial Lung Disease (likely due to metal dust/fumes exposure). Given the discrepancy between the X-ray findings and the previous COPD note, I recommend a High-Resolution CT (HRCT) to confirm the fibrotic pattern and a Pulmonary Function Test (PFT) to assess severity.
